label: <DEL> step of length-9 sequences (first-token dependent)
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L), almost entirely when L == 9 (96% of mass; the rest is L == 8, never L <= 7, never in the original or copy phases). Within L == 9 delimiter steps only ~19% are active, so precision is low. Which ones fire depends on the first original tokens in a distributed way: first token z/3/p/2/r/w/k/g/b and second token b/3/f/s/p/u/z/q raise the rate and magnitude (requiring both gives precision 0.63 but recall 0.24; either one gives recall 0.77, mass recall 0.85, precision 0.33). Activations are tiny in absolute terms (max 0.004). No compact token rule found, so the selectivity within L=9 delimiter steps is unexplained.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: z, 3, p, w, 2, r; least: y, x, i, 0) and the third original token (most: f, s, b, 3, u, p; least: o, w, 2, k); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, to_go=8, t=9.
